In the written statement , respondent No.1/ insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Car bearing No.KA-01-MJ-0739 , however, denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.2 on the ground that respondent No.2 violated driver clause of the policy by authorizing a boy aged about 16 years who had no licence to drive the car.

Hence, it is clear that respondent No.2 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-01- MJ-0739 has violated the driver clause of the policy by authorizing Thoushiff pasha , a minor to drive the car without licence.
Hence, respondent No.2 owner of the car is not eligible to be indemnified by respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

The petitions registered as M.V.C.No.5824/2022 and M.V.C.No.5825/2022 filed under Section 166 of IMV Act are hereby partly allowed.

In M.V.C.No.5824/2022, the respondent No.2 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-01-MJ-0739 shall pay Rs.42,41,000/- (Rupees forty two lakhs forty one thousand only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners No.1 to 4 towards compensation.

In M.V.C.No.5825/2022, the respondent No.2 shall pay Rs.3,60,154/- (Rupees three lakhs sixty thousand one hundred and fifty four only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner Prasenjit Midya towards compensation.
